symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Known fixed rank of the graphon kernel.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Known bound on response levels and derivatives through order two.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Known uniform \(C^3\) radius for exposure responses.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Fixed bound for kernel size and expected-degree regularity.

symbols.name: \underline\lambda
symbols.def: Fixed lower bound on nonzero graphon eigenvalues in magnitude.

symbols.name: C_{\log}
symbols.def: Fixed lower constant in the sparse-degree window.

symbols.name: b_\psi
symbols.def: Fixed moment parameter for graphon eigenfunctions.

symbols.name: f_i
symbols.def: Unit \(i\)'s response as a function of own treatment and treated-neighbor fraction.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Observed symmetric adjacency matrix with zero diagonal.

symbols.name: N
symbols.def: Generic integer degree used to define the exact lattice radius.

symbols.name: Y_i(z)
symbols.def: Potential outcome of unit \(i\) under assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: \bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}
symbols.def: Finite Bernoulli-policy indirect-effect estimand defined in \({\rm def:li-wager-target}\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: Common localization bandwidth before exact degree adaptation.

symbols.name: \delta_N
symbols.def: Exact distance from one half to the nearest nonzero point on the degree-\(N\) exposure lattice, defined in \({\rm def:lattice-radius}\).

symbols.name: \mu_{2,i}(h)
symbols.def: Conditional binomial moment defined in \({\rm def:discrete-score}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Psi_r(A)
symbols.def: Matrix of the \(\min\{r,n\}\) eigenvectors of \(A\) with eigenvalues largest in magnitude, selected by the deterministic convention in \({\rm def:empirical\text{-}projector}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Pi_r(A)
symbols.def: Orthogonal projector onto the deterministically selected leading \(\min\{r,n\}\) eigenspace of \(A\), defined in \({\rm def:empirical\text{-}projector}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
symbols.def: Nonnegative graph-observable residualization certificate returned by the PC construction.

symbols.name: \widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}
symbols.def: Nonnegative graph-observable variance remainder returned by the PC construction.

symbols.name: \overline s_h(A)
symbols.def: Degree-exact standard-deviation radius defined in \({\rm def:radii}\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: Generic probability law in the maintained graphon-response class.

symbols.name: h^\dagger
symbols.def: Oracle full-class radius-minimizing bandwidth, defined in \({\rm def:exact-optimal-bandwidth}\) only when both the bandwidth set and model class are nonempty.

symbols.name: \mathfrak u_{n,d,L}
symbols.def: Oracle conservative worst-case expected graph-observable radius at \(h^\dagger\), defined in \({\rm def:frontier-envelope}\) only when both the bandwidth set and model class are nonempty.

symbols.name: \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
symbols.def: Honest expected interval-length criterion defined in \({\rm def:minimax\text{-}criteria}\).

symbols.name: h_0
symbols.def: Balance point \(h_0=(L^{-2}/(n\sqrt d))^{1/7}\) for \(L>0\), and \(h_0=\infty\) for \(L=0\).

symbols.name: Q_{i,h}
symbols.def: Finite degree-lattice maximum of the absolute exact score for unit \(i\) and bandwidth \(h\), defined in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\).

symbols.name: D_{ij,h}
symbols.def: Finite degree-lattice maximum change in unit \(i\)'s exact score when assignment coordinate \(j\) is flipped, defined in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\).

symbols.name: \Gamma_{i,h}
symbols.def: Observable uniform bound on the absolute feasible PC-balanced score for unit \(i\) and bandwidth \(h\), defined in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\).

symbols.name: \beta_{ij,h}
symbols.def: Observable bound on the change in unit \(i\)'s score--outcome product when assignment coordinate \(j\) is flipped, defined in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\).

symbols.name: \widehat h(A)
symbols.def: Smallest graph-observable finite-candidate certificate minimizer defined in \({\rm def:operational\text{-}bandwidth}\).

standard.name: Independent Bernoulli randomization at probability one half

assumptions.condition: \((U_i,f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\) are independent and identically distributed preassignment draws from a joint law whose \(U_i\)-marginal is \({\rm Uniform}[0,1]\).

standard.name: Li--Wager independent unit-type and response sampling with uniform latent types

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \((U_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the variables \((A_{ij})_{i<j}\) are independent with \(A_{ij}\sim{\rm Bernoulli}(\rho_nW(U_i,U_j))\), \(A_{ji}=A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\).
Each \(\psi_k(U_i)\) satisfies Bernstein's moment condition with parameter \(b_\psi\) for \(1\le k\le r\).

standard.name: Li--Wager bounded response and derivative envelope through order two
Known \(C^3\) radius separated from the lower-order response envelope

definitions.name: Maintained known-rank \(C^3\) graphon class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}=\{P_{n,d,L}:\text{ every condition in the displayed member-property list holds for }P_{n,d,L}\text{ at triangular-array index }n\}\).  This is the maintained bounded, row-regular, known-rank, two-radius graphon class selected by exactly those properties.  It is neither identified with nor contained in the full Theorem~4/6 regime of LiWager2022RandomGraph; only the intersection of the two regimes is used for comparison.  In particular, \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d\) and \(d/n\to0\) do not imply the source condition \(-1/2<\liminf_n\log(\rho_n)/\log n\), and the displayed member properties do not reproduce every source condition.

definitions.name: Li--Wager finite indirect-effect benchmark
definitions.construction: At Bernoulli probability one half, \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}=4n^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbb E_Z[Y_i(Z)(M_i-N_i/2)\mid A,(f_j)_{j\in\mathcal V_n}]\), equivalently the finite indirect effect in equation (1) of LiWager2022RandomGraph.

definitions.name: Exact realized-degree support correction
definitions.construction: For \(N\ge1\), set \(\delta_N=N^{-1}\) when \(N\) is even and \(\delta_N=(2N)^{-1}\) when \(N\) is odd; for each \(i\) with \(N_i>0\), set \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact symmetric discrete local-polynomial score
definitions.construction: For \(N_i>0\), let \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=\mathbb E_Z[V_i^2\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}\mid A]\) and \(q_{i,h}=V_i\mathbf 1\{|V_i|\le h_i(h)\}/\mu_{2,i}(h)\). For \(N_i=0\), set \(q_{i,h}=0\) and \(\mu_{2,i}(h)=0\).

definitions.name: Deterministically selected observed principal-component projector
definitions.construction:
Put \(m_{r,n}=\min\{r,n\}\).  Order the \(n\) eigenvalues of the symmetric matrix \(A\) by decreasing absolute value, breaking equal-absolute-value ties by decreasing signed value.  Within every remaining repeated eigenspace, choose the orthonormal basis obtained by applying Gram--Schmidt to the nonzero vectors in the ordered list of projections of \(e_1,\ldots,e_n\) onto that eigenspace.  Let \(\widehat\Psi_r(A)\in\mathbb R^{n\times m_{r,n}}\) contain the first \(m_{r,n}\) resulting orthonormal eigenvectors and define
\[
 \widehat\Pi_r(A)=\widehat\Psi_r(A)\widehat\Psi_r(A)^\top.
\]
Thus \(\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) is the orthogonal spectral projector onto the leading \(\min\{r,n\}\)-dimensional eigenspace selected by this convention.  The deterministic tie rule makes \(A\mapsto\widehat\Pi_r(A)\) a fixed Borel-measurable sample map for every \(r,n\in\mathbb N\), without requiring \(r\leq n\).

definitions.name: Explicit first-projection PC handle with bounded-difference certificate
Feasible explicit first-projection PC estimator
definitions.construction:
With the explicit score from \({\rm def:pc-handle}\),
\[
 \widehat\theta_h
 =\frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}
 \left[q_{i,h}-4\left\{\widehat\Pi_r(A)A
       (Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n)\right\}_i\right]Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]

definitions.name: Graph-observable degree-exact radii for the explicit PC handle
definitions.construction:
For the explicit certificates in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), set
\[
 \overline b_h(A)=\frac{L}{6n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}
 +\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}
\]
and
\[
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\]
Thus \(\overline s_h(A)\) is a finite-sample conditional standard-deviation certificate, not an asserted sharp-rate formula.

definitions.name: Exact-support exponential bounded-difference interval
definitions.construction:
Put
\[
 a_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)},\qquad
 R_h(A)=\overline b_h(A)+a_\alpha\overline s_h(A),
\]
\[
 L_h=\widehat\theta_h-R_h(A),\qquad
 U_h=\widehat\theta_h+R_h(A),\qquad
 \operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(t)=\max\{-B,\min\{B,t\}\}.
\]
Define the unprojected interval \(\mathcal J_h=[L_h,U_h]\) and the reported interval
\[
 \mathcal C_h=
 [\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(L_h),
  \operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(U_h)].
\]
Thus \(\mathcal C_h\) is the endpointwise monotone projection of \(\mathcal J_h\) onto the known parameter range.

definitions.name: Oracle degree-exact optimal base bandwidth
definitions.construction:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), define
\[
 h^\dagger=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)].
\]
This is the oracle full-class radius-minimizing bandwidth.  Its evaluation requires the full-class supremum and is not an operational data-driven tuning rule.

definitions.name: Supported and oracle degree-exact full-class envelopes
Nonempty-class absolute-risk and honest expected interval-length criteria
definitions.construction: At every index for which \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), let \(D=(A,Z,(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}})_{i\in\mathcal V_n})\). Define \(R^*_{n,d,L}=\inf_{\widetilde\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P|\widetilde\theta-\theta_n|\), where the infimum ranges over all real-valued measurable estimators \(\widetilde\theta=\widetilde\theta(D)\). Define \(\Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)=\inf_{\mathcal C}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}\mathbb E_P[u(D)-\ell(D)]\), where the infimum ranges over data-measurable closed intervals \(\mathcal C(D)=[\ell(D),u(D)]\) with finite measurable endpoints \(\ell(D)\leq u(D)\) and satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C(D)\}\geq1-\alpha\). For every such interval, \(\operatorname{length}\{\mathcal C(D)\}=u(D)-\ell(D)\).

definitions.name: Graph-observable finite-breakpoint operational bandwidth
definitions.construction:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), put \(\ell=d^{-1}\), \(u=\min\{d^{-1/2},1/2\}\), and, for each realized graph \(A\), define the finite nonempty candidate set
\[
 \mathcal K(A)=\{\ell,u\}\cup
 \left\{\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|:
 i\in\mathcal V_n,\ N_i>0,\ 0\leq m\leq N_i,\
 \ell\leq\left|\frac m{N_i}-\frac12\right|\leq u\right\}.
\]
The graph-adaptive operational bandwidth is
\[
 \widehat h(A)=\min\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\mathcal K(A)}
 \{\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\}.
\]
All ties are therefore resolved deterministically toward the smallest candidate.  The construction uses only the observed graph, the known constants, and the finite-lattice certificates; it does not use \(Z\) or the observed outcomes.

statements.statement: For every \(i\in\mathcal V_n\) with \(N_i\ge1\) and every \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), the exact support correction gives \(\mu_{2,i}(h)>0\). Symmetry of \(M_i\sim{\rm Binomial}(N_i,1/2)\) yields \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}\mid A]=0\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i\mid A]=1\), \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}V_i^2\mid A]=0\), and \(\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}^2\mid A]=\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\). For each \(a\in\{0,1\}\), \(|\mathbb E_Z[q_{i,h}f_i(a,1/2+V_i)\mid A]-\partial_xf_i(a,1/2)|\le Lh_i(h)^2/6\).
statements.justification: This establishes exact derivative moments at every positive realized degree and removes the zero-normalizer failure at the lower bandwidth endpoint.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph uses an unlocalized global binomial score; ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest does not face a random degree lattice.
statements.consumer: It supplies the unitwise bias and exact inverse-moment contribution in the feasible-PC certificate.

statements.statement:
Conditional on \(A\) and \((f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\), the derivative target and the Li--Wager finite indirect effect satisfy
\[
 \left|\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n\right|
 \le \frac{L}{8n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac{1}{N_i}
 +\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\mathbf 1\{N_i=0\}.
\]
Moreover, along any maintained triangular-array sequence with fixed \(B\) and \(\kappa\) such that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\log(\rho_n)/\log(n)>-1/2\), one has \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}-\theta_n=o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\). On the further intersection of such a sequence with every source hypothesis enumerated in \({\rm lem:li-wager-theorem-six-regime}\), specialize the treatment probability to one half and, writing \(\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) for the nonnegative variance factor in the full standardizer \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) of Li--Wager's equation~(43) at the \(n\)-th law, additionally suppose that \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\). Then the equation~(43) Gaussian limit centered at \(\bar\tau_{\mathrm{IND},n}\) transfers by an additive Slutsky argument to the same statistic centered at \(\theta_n\). This is an asymptotic comparator only on that intersection, not a theorem for every sequence in \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), and it is not a finite-sample equality of the two targets.
statements.justification: The bridge separates a maintained-class center approximation from use of the published Gaussian theorem, so the latter is invoked only where every source condition holds.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph Proposition~1 gives a minimum-degree approximation; the displayed degree-exact symmetric remainder keeps isolates visible and does not identify the two finite-sample targets. Its Theorem~6 applies only under the full source conditions recorded in the cited lemma.
statements.consumer: It permits asymptotic comparison with Li--Wager equation~(43) only on the stated class intersection while keeping the finite-population derivative as a distinct target everywhere.

statements.statement: Using \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), construct in polynomial time \(\widetilde\gamma_h(A,Z)\), \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\), and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}\), simultaneously for all \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\), such that the estimator has conditional absolute bias at most \(\overline b_h(A)\), conditional variance at most \(\overline s_h(A)^2\), and the resulting interval has unconditional coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) over every \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\). Establish \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L})\) and \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=O_P(d/n)\) uniformly from \(d\asymp\log n\) through \(d=o(n)\), or determine the first larger bandwidth-dependent term forced by feasible spectral residualization.
statements.justification: The empirical-projector step is where localization can create an additional term, so the estimator and both observable PC remainders remain the first-class open construction.
statements.gap: LiWager2022RandomGraph proves a global-score projector expansion in a denser polynomial-degree window; AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise does not propagate eigenvector error through exact-support causal weights.
statements.consumer: A positive or corrected answer gives a feasible bias and variance certificate for one sparse professional-network experiment.

statements.statement:
At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), the graph-observable selector \(\widehat h(A)\) is well defined, Borel measurable, and polynomial-time computable.  For every prespecified \(h\in\mathcal H_{n,d}\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), the feasible estimator and interval satisfy
\[
 \Pr_Z\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_h\mid A,(f_i)_{i\in\mathcal V_n}\}\geq1-\alpha
\]
for almost every preassignment realization, and the same conditional guarantee holds after the graph-adaptive choice \(h=\widehat h(A)\).  Before endpoint clipping to \([-B,B]\), the pointwise half-length is exactly
\[
 \overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)},
\]
including every realized degree and isolate.  In particular, \(h=d^{-1}\) is admissible whenever \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\), while \(\widehat h(A)\) is the operational certificate-minimizing choice.

At every index for which both \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), the class-level oracle bandwidth \(h^\dagger\) is well defined and is used only as a comparison object.  The pointwise candidate inequality implies the operational integrated bounds
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P|\widehat\theta_{\widehat h(A)}-\theta_n|
 \leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)}\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d,L}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{\widehat h(A)})]
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
No comparison \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\), sharp minimax rate, or achieved honest expected-length frontier is asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem converts the graph-only finite-breakpoint selector into selection-valid conditional inference and operational integrated guarantees, while retaining the class oracle only as a comparison object.
statements.gap: The graph-adaptive rule minimizes the observable certificate, but no theorem compares its conservative full-class envelope with the supported analytic lower benchmark.
statements.consumer: Experimenters may report the selected exponential interval directly; its risk and expected length are bounded by the conservative envelope without pretending that envelope is rate sharp.

statements.statement:
For \(1\leq k\leq r\), let \(I_k=[(k-1)/r,k/r)\), with \(1\) included in \(I_r\), put \(\psi_k(u)=\sqrt r\,\mathbf 1\{u\in I_k\}\), and set
\[
 c_0=\max\{r/\kappa,r\underline\lambda\},
 \qquad
 W_0(u,v)=c_0\mathbf 1\{u\text{ and }v\text{ belong to the same }I_k\}.
\]
Suppose, in addition to the conditions defining \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\), that
\[
 c_0\leq\kappa,
 \qquad
 b_\psi\geq (r-1)/\sqrt r.
\]
Let \(s_0=B/4\), let \(\xi_i\) be i.i.d. with density \(p_{s_0}(t)=s_0^{-1}\cos^2(\pi t/(2s_0))\mathbf 1\{|t|\leq s_0\}\), and use response pairs \(f_i^\pm(a,x)=\xi_i\pm g(x)\), with the three functions \(g\) constructed in the proof.  Then \(W_0\) and these random-intercept response laws generate an explicit block submodel of \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\).  Along sequences with \(B,L,r,\kappa,\underline\lambda,b_\psi,\alpha,C_{\log}\) fixed and \(C_{\log}\log n\leq d=o(n)\), there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(n\) and \(d\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Within this same block submodel, respectively, a degree-lattice bump, an interior \(C^3\) bump, and a linear response pair furnish the lattice term, the interior nonlinear term for both absolute risk and honest expected length, and the graph floor.  The two displayed compatibility inequalities are only sufficient conditions for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same supported lower benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.justification: The explicit equal-block graphon and three same-class response pairs prove the supported analytic converse under the displayed sufficient compatibility conditions; \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) separately proves the same benchmark over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.gap: The compatibility inequalities are merely sufficient for this explicit block witness and do not characterize nonemptiness. This is a limitation of the witness, not a gap in the supported lower benchmark, which \({\rm thm:unrestricted\text{-}supported\text{-}converse}\) establishes over every eventually nonempty repaired class.
statements.consumer: Experimenters may use the supported bandwidth envelope as a certified global lower benchmark whenever the repaired class is eventually nonempty; this theorem additionally provides a concrete equal-block witness when its displayed compatibility conditions hold.

statements.statement:
For \(L>0\), at every sufficiently large triangular-array index the supported-unit component satisfies \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp Ld^{-2}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\leq d^{-1}\), \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp L^{3/7}(n^2d)^{-1/7}+\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(d^{-1}<h_0<d^{-1/2}\), and \(\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\asymp\sqrt{d/n}\) when \(h_0\geq d^{-1/2}\).  At every index for which \(\mathcal H_{n,d}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal M_{n,d,L}\ne\varnothing\), the operational graph-adaptive selector satisfies
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\leq\mathfrak u_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)
 \leq2\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)}\,\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}.
\]
Along every sequence covered by the unrestricted supported converse, there is a constant \(c>0\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 R^*_{n,d,L}\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L},
 \qquad
 \Lambda^*_{n,d,L}(\alpha)\geq c\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}.
\]
Every graph-only conditional-bias certificate over the maintained class retains at least \(Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}\) on a realized graph.  The explicit compatible block-submodel lower bound transfers upward only to the maintained class, and the unrestricted converse proves the maintained-class lower benchmark directly; neither result transfers automatically to the nonnested LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem~6 regime or its distinct finite indirect-effect target.  No bound \(\mathfrak u_{n,d,L}\lesssim\mathfrak r^{\mathrm{sup}}_{n,d,L}\) is proved, so the three analytic phases remain tuning geometry and a minimax lower benchmark rather than a sharp or achieved frontier.
statements.justification: This proposition solves the analytic tuning geometry and combines the same-class lower benchmark with an operational graph-adaptive conservative upper envelope.
statements.gap: The bounded-difference certificate has no proved comparison with the analytic supported envelope, so the displayed operational bracket is not known to be tight.
statements.consumer: The three phases support design triage only as lower-benchmark and tuning geometry; the graph-adaptive upper curve is reportable but remains conservative.

sampling_model.units: One triangular-array population with independent preassignment draws \((U_i,f_i)\); the finite-population derivative is realized after this draw.
sampling_model.network: One observed undirected graph drawn conditionally independently from the sparse finite-rank graphon \(\rho_nW\), with \(\rho_n=d/n\).
sampling_model.treatment: Own treatment is independent of the neighbor count conditional on the preassignment graph.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment probability is known and fixed at one half; each positive realized degree uses its exact nearest nonzero exposure support, and isolates remain explicitly unsupported.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Graphon eigenfunctions are replaced by the leading empirical eigenspace; leave-one-edge-out residualization returns observable bias and variance remainder certificates.
sampling_model.inference_randomness: Coverage and risk average over the declared preassignment unit draw, graph draw, and Bernoulli assignment, as in the retained model; graph-observable radii expose the realized support contribution.

estimand_functional:
\(X=Z-\tfrac12\mathbf1_n,\quad P_A=\widehat\Pi_r(A),\quad C_A=P_AA,\quad \widetilde\gamma_{i,h}=q_{i,h}-4(C_AX)_i,\quad \widehat\theta_h=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\widetilde\gamma_{i,h}Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\), with \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\).  The bias certificate is
\[
 \widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}=\frac{2B}{n}\sum_i|(C_A)_{ii}|+\frac{B}{n}\sum_{i:N_i>0}\frac1{N_i}\sum_{j:A_{ij}=1}|(C_A)_{ij}|,
\]
while \(Q_{i,h}\), \(D_{ij,h}\), \(\Gamma_{i,h}\), and \(\beta_{ij,h}\) are the finite-lattice maxima and coordinate-oscillation bounds in \({\rm def:pc-handle}\), and
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}=\frac1{4n^2}\sum_j\left(\sum_i\beta_{ij,h}\right)^2,
 \qquad
 \overline s_h(A)^2=\widehat V_{\mathrm{pc},h}.
\]
The bias radius is \(\overline b_h(A)=L(6n)^{-1}\sum_{i:N_i>0}h_i(h)^2+Bn^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1\{N_i=0\}+\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{pc},h}\).  The operational bandwidth \(\widehat h(A)\) is the smallest minimizer of \(\overline b_h(A)+\overline s_h(A)\) over the finite graph-observable candidate set in \({\rm def:operational\text{-}bandwidth}\).  For either a prespecified \(h\) or \(h=\widehat h(A)\), put
\[
 a_\alpha=\sqrt{2\log(2/\alpha)},\qquad R_h(A)=\overline b_h(A)+a_\alpha\overline s_h(A),
\]
\[
 L_h=\widehat\theta_h-R_h(A),\qquad U_h=\widehat\theta_h+R_h(A),\qquad \operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(t)=\max\{-B,\min\{B,t\}\}.
\]
The reportable interval is
\[
 \mathcal C_h=[\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(L_h),\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]}(U_h)].

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 6, equations (40)--(43), under the conditions of Theorem 4, gives a Gaussian limit at \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\) scale for its principal-component-balancing estimator centered at its population and finite indirect effects.
Theorem 2.1 and Section 3 incorporate worst-case smoothness bias into honest fixed-length confidence intervals and bandwidth choice in nonparametric regression.
Theorems 1--3 use between-class and ordered moduli to bound expected length of honest adaptive confidence intervals.
The average direct and indirect effects decompose the derivative of Bernoulli policy value.
Theorem 2.1 supplies entrywise first-order eigenvector approximations for low-expected-rank random matrices.
Two-to-infinity expansions and rank-adaptive testing are available for possibly infinite-rank latent-position random graphs.
Approximate-neighborhood interference supports inference for causal level effects under locality conditions.
The paper studies design-based minimax risk on a fixed observed network over all designs and estimators for arbitrary neighborhood interference, including direct and global effects.
The paper fixes a Bernoulli design and studies the total treatment effect under low-order polynomial interactions.

The paper develops design-based asymptotic theory under Bernoulli assignment for Horvitz--Thompson estimators of direct, indirect, and total average treatment effects under uniformly bounded neighbourhood interference, and proposes eigenvector-adjusted point estimators and variance estimators. In contrast, the present note uses a stochastic sparse-graphon model, targets a midpoint derivative on exact realized-degree lattices, proves a finite-sample graph-observable conditional certificate, and gives a same-class smoothness-dependent minimax expected-length lower benchmark without proving a matching feasible upper rate.

tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the new finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, the graph dependence term, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit frontier retains lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. A same-class testing calculation gives only \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) for isolates, whereas the safe interval pays \(B\pi_{0,n}\); therefore no full matched-frontier theorem is claimed. The open content is uniform feasible-PC certification and tail-adaptive completion without minimum-degree or response-sharing assumptions. Li and Wager's Theorem 6 is used only through an explicit finite-to-derivative bridge as an asymptotic benchmark.

project_justification.gap: Li and Wager prove asymptotic normality for a PC estimator of their finite and population indirect effects, but they do not give finite-sample honest length for the distinct realized derivative target or handle exact low-degree support. Standard honest nonparametric theory has no random exposure lattice, graph projector, or latent-type-dependent isolate tail.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a degree-exact, bias-aware statistical frontier for a causal derivative from one network, with observable support diagnostics and an honest distinction between conservative isolate bias and the same-class testing modulus.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact score moments at every positive degree, proves a finite-sample bridge to the published indirect effect, constructs PC-balanced observable radii, establishes supported-unit upper and lower rates plus a degree-tail modulus, and isolates the one remaining tail-adaptation question instead of asserting a false matched frontier.

related_work: LiWager2022RandomGraph is the central asymptotic benchmark. Proposition 1, equations (4)--(5), relates its finite indirect effect to an average derivative through a minimum-degree remainder, and Theorem 6, equation (43), gives a \(\sqrt{\rho_n}\)-scale Gaussian limit for its PC estimator in a polynomial-degree sparse regime. The present target \(\theta_n\) is a new realized finite-population derivative; \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\) gives the exact degree-level comparison, so no finite-sample same-target tightening is claimed. HuLiWager2022AverageDirectIndirect supplies the Bernoulli-policy decomposition and causal interpretation. ArmstrongKolesar2020SimpleHonest informs the computable smoothness-bias interval geometry, while CaiLow2004Adaptation informs the testing-to-expected-length argument; neither treats network support or spectral residualization. AbbeFanWangZhong2020Entrywise and TangCape2025InfiniteRank inform the empirical-eigenspace analysis but do not control an exact-support causal score. Leung2022NetworkInference concerns locality-based inference for level effects. BhadraSchweinberger2025Survey is cited only as a broad survey of network-interference frameworks; the separate arXiv identifier 2504.06108 is omitted because its current contagion manuscript is not the linear-rate comparator described in the earlier core.
technical_internal_limitation: For \(N_i>0\), the exact score has second moment \(\mu_{2,i}(h)^{-1}\) and third-order bias at most \(Lh_i(h)^2/6\). These identities do not establish the feasible spectral remainders. Isolates have no exposure variation, so the safe interval adds their full derivative envelope. Under i.i.d. preassignment responses, the corresponding same-class testing modulus is smaller, of order \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\); closing that upper--lower gap requires an estimator, not a stronger assumption.
honest_scope: The finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) is the target. LiWager2022RandomGraph Theorem 6 is only an asymptotic benchmark after \({\rm prop:li-wager-bridge}\). Every positive realized degree is handled by its exact support radius; isolates remain visible in the certificate. The supported-unit lattice, interior, and graph-floor terms have a proposed matching converse, and the same-class unsupported and low-degree modulus is explicit. A full matched frontier is not claimed because the safe \(B\pi_{0,n}\) upper allowance is not matched by the \(B\sqrt{\pi_{0,n}/n}\) isolate testing term. The open tail-adaptive construction must retain the i.i.d. \((U_i,f_i)\) class and the stated conditioning convention. Unknown rank, unknown \(L\), simultaneous policy bands, and optimal ego-cluster design remain outside scope.
